cell_type_model: ZNRF3 ectodomain assays; Lgr5+ intestinal organoids; WNT reporter cells
assay_or_perturbation: Fu1-Fu2 binding/SPR; Rspo perturbation; WNT reporter and organoid self-renewal assays
relation_type: exact RSPO3-ZNRF3 ligand binding with receptor-proximal inhibition of Frizzled turnover and canonical WNT activation
pathway_branch: RSPO3-ZNRF3 -> reduced Frizzled ubiquitination/turnover -> WNT-beta-catenin/TCF-LEF activity
limitations: Direct RSPO3-ZNRF3 binding is strongest in ectodomain/ligand panels; RNF43 evidence is not transferred to this row. ZNRF3 is a membrane E3 ligase complex component rather than a classical kinase receptor; reporter/organoid endpoints do not prove every intermediate.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells stably expressing human LGR6
assay_or_perturbation: Whole-cell competition binding with RSPO1-4; RSPO4 activity comparison in LGR6-expressing cells
relation_type: exact high-affinity RSPO4-LGR6 binding without a resolved productive LGR6-specific relay
pathway_branch: RSPO4-LGR6 binding; no LGR6-specific WNT potentiation resolved
limitations: LGR6 binding is specific and high affinity, but LGR6 overexpression did not enhance RSPO4 activity in the tested system. LGR4/LGR5 or other RSPO-family function is not substituted for this exact pair.

cell_type_model: Rnf43 ectodomain binding; intestinal organoids; WNT reporter cells
assay_or_perturbation: Rspo4-Rnf43 ECD binding; R-spondin perturbation; WNT reporter and organoid assays
relation_type: exact RSPO4-RNF43 ligand binding with receptor-proximal protection of Frizzled and canonical WNT potentiation
pathway_branch: RSPO4-RNF43 -> reduced Frizzled turnover -> WNT-beta-catenin/TCF-LEF activity
limitations: RSPO4 is a weaker ZNRF3/RNF43 ligand in some biochemical assays and potency varies with construct and assay. Structural family-level RSPO/ZNRF3 information is used only as mechanism context; the exact RSPO4-RNF43 result is from the binding panel.

cell_type_model: Znrf3 ectodomain binding; intestinal organoids; WNT reporter cells
assay_or_perturbation: Rspo4-Znrf3 ECD binding/affinity; R-spondin perturbation; WNT reporter and organoid assays
relation_type: exact RSPO4-ZNRF3 ligand binding with receptor-proximal protection of Frizzled and canonical WNT potentiation
pathway_branch: RSPO4-ZNRF3 -> reduced Frizzled turnover -> WNT-beta-catenin/TCF-LEF activity
limitations: RSPO4 binding and activity are comparatively weak and construct-dependent. RNF43 evidence is not promoted into this exact ZNRF3 row; downstream reporter/organoid function supports pathway output, not a direct intracellular RSPO4-ZNRF3 signal.

cell_type_model: primary neurons; NgR1/NGFR/p75/LINGO1 receptor-complex systems
assay_or_perturbation: Nogo-66/RTN4 neurite-inhibition assays; coexpression and genetic loss of receptor-complex subunits; RhoA readouts
relation_type: exact receptor-complex relay assignment: RTN4/Nogo-66 engages an NgR1-RTN4R-NGFR/p75-LINGO1 complex, with NGFR as signal-transducing subunit rather than demonstrated ligand-binding subunit
pathway_branch: RTN4-NgR1/NGFR/LINGO1 -> RhoA-ROCK and cytoskeletal inhibition -> neurite growth/plasticity
limitations: Direct binary RTN4-NGFR binding is not established; direct ligand-binding evidence is for RTN4R/NgR1. Genetic studies differ by neuronal context, and Nogo-A domain/isoform matters.

cell_type_model: NgR1/RTN4R ectodomain; primary neurons; Nogo receptor-complex cells
assay_or_perturbation: Nogo-A/RTN4 domain mapping; binding and receptor-complex assays; neurite outgrowth and RhoA/Rho-kinase inhibition
relation_type: exact RTN4-NgR1/RTN4R ligand binding and receptor-complex signaling
pathway_branch: RTN4-NgR1/RTN4R-NGFR/LINGO1 -> RhoA-ROCK/cytoskeleton -> neurite inhibition and plasticity
limitations: The direct interaction is domain- and isoform-dependent, with the Nogo-66 region as the principal mapped ligand. NGFR/LINGO1 are required complex context but are not interchangeable with the exact RTN4R edge.

cell_type_model: neurons; hippocampal synapses; stroke-model tissue; S1PR2-expressing cells
assay_or_perturbation: Nogo-A-Delta20/S1PR2 Y2H and co-IP; binding; pharmacologic/genetic S1PR2 blockade; RhoA and synaptic plasticity assays
relation_type: exact RTN4/Nogo-A-S1PR2 binding and GPCR-proximal signaling
pathway_branch: RTN4/Nogo-A-Delta20-S1PR2 -> G13-LARG-RhoA/ROCK -> neurite inhibition and reduced synaptic plasticity
limitations: The active ligand is the Nogo-A Delta20 region, not an undifferentiated RTN4 isoform. S1PR2 is a sphingolipid GPCR with context-dependent ligand occupancy; downstream tissue phenotypes are not transcription-factor endpoints.

cell_type_model: ischemic cardiomyocytes; cardiac fibroblasts; hypoxic cardiomyocytes
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant/released S100A1; Tlr4/MyD88 knockout and pharmacologic controls; MAPK/SAPK and p65 assays; myocardial injury models
relation_type: exact TLR4-dependent S100A1 DAMP activation with downstream NF-kappaB/MAPK response
pathway_branch: S100A1-TLR4/MyD88 -> MAPK/SAPK and RELA/p65 -> cardiac-fibroblast inflammatory/anti-fibrotic response
limitations: The study establishes receptor dependence and a cellular response rather than a purified S100A1-TLR4/MD-2 affinity measurement. Findings are ischemia/cardiac-context specific and do not establish a universal TLR4 complex stoichiometry.

cell_type_model: primary hippocampal and dopaminergic neurons; ErbB-expressing cells
assay_or_perturbation: label-transfer cross-linking and SPR; ErbB inhibition/knockdown; neuronal survival and neurite assays
relation_type: exact S100A4-ErbB3 binding, with downstream survival assigned to ErbB4/ErbB2 rather than isolated ErbB3 relay
pathway_branch: S100A4-ErbB3 binding; broader S100A4-ErbB4/ErbB2-Akt neuroprotection is not an ErbB3-specific edge
limitations: SPR supports direct S100A4-ErbB3 interaction, but functional neuroprotection was dependent mainly on ErbB4/ErbB2 and Akt. No ErbB3-specific downstream endpoint is isolated; family ErbB analogy is not used to promote this row.

cell_type_model: CD36-overexpressing HeLa cells; primary rat macrophages/Kupffer cells; airway macrophages
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-SAA binding and uptake; CD36 gain/loss and blocking; JNK/ERK, NF-kappaB/MAPK, cytokine and macrophage-function assays
relation_type: exact SAA1-CD36 binding and scavenger-receptor signaling
pathway_branch: SAA1-CD36 -> JNK/ERK and NF-kappaB/MAPK -> macrophage activation/dysfunction and inflammatory remodeling
limitations: Direct binding is shown in overexpression and primary-cell systems, but SAA preparations, receptor complexes, and CD36 scavenging/internalization complicate stoichiometry. NF-kappaB pathway activation was not assigned to a single measured terminal TF.

cell_type_model: RBL-FPR2 cells; primary leukocytes; chemotaxis systems
assay_or_perturbation: SAA1 isoform stimulation; FPR2-dependent calcium, ERK and chemotaxis assays; HPLC purification and receptor controls
relation_type: exact SAA1-FPR2 activation with GPCR-proximal calcium/ERK and chemotaxis output
pathway_branch: SAA1-FPR2 -> calcium/ERK signaling -> leukocyte chemotaxis and inflammatory activation
limitations: SAA1 isoform and preparation purity materially affect potency; purified-protein work supports FPR2 activity but does not establish a single structural binding mode. Downstream endpoints are cellular, not terminal-TF measurements.

cell_type_model: RBL-FPR2 cells; neutrophils; hepatocyte-colorectal cancer co-culture and liver-metastasis model
assay_or_perturbation: SAA2.2 isoform stimulation with FPR2 calcium/ERK/chemotaxis assays; cancer-cell/hepatocyte conditioned media; FPR2 perturbation and Egr1 transcriptional readouts
relation_type: exact SAA2-FPR2 activation with chemotaxis and a measured EGR1 transcriptional endpoint
pathway_branch: SAA2-FPR2 -> PI3K-AKT and chemotaxis -> EGR1-driven neutrophil transcriptional program
limitations: The direct receptor assays use SAA2.2, whereas the newer in vivo model involves mouse hepatocyte-derived SAA2 and tumor-conditioned signaling. The EGR1 handoff is model-specific; purified SAA2-FPR2 affinity is not established in the metastasis study.

cell_type_model: TLR2 reporter cells; macrophages; recombinant acute-phase SAA preparations
assay_or_perturbation: SAA2.2 TLR2-dependent reporter/cytokine assays; comparison of isoforms; endotoxin/lipoprotein contamination controls and reconstitution studies
relation_type: SAA2-TLR2 productive edge remains unresolved despite receptor-proximal reporter evidence
pathway_branch: SAA2/TLR2 NF-kappaB reporter boundary; later contamination studies challenge attribution of native SAA stimulation to TLR2
limitations: No purified SAA2-TLR2 affinity or definitive binary interaction is available. Results depend on isoform and recombinant preparation, and bacterial lipoproteins can account for TLR2-stimulating activity; SAA1 evidence is not transferred to exact Saa2.

cell_type_model: vascular endothelial cells; endothelial-specific Scube2 knockout mice
assay_or_perturbation: co-IP and ligand-binding assays; SCUBE2 overexpression/shRNA; VEGF stimulation; VEGFR2 phosphorylation, MAPK/AKT and angiogenesis assays
relation_type: exact SCUBE2-KDR/VEGFR2 coreceptor-complex interaction in VEGF signaling
pathway_branch: SCUBE2-VEGF-KDR/VEGFR2 -> receptor phosphorylation -> MAPK/AKT -> endothelial growth, tube formation and neovascularization
limitations: SCUBE2 is a coreceptor/complex component and does not replace VEGF as the primary KDR ligand. KDR binding is strongest in the VEGF-containing ternary context; no terminal transcription factor was directly established.

cell_type_model: mouse T cells and CD7-expressing cells; human T-cell migration models
assay_or_perturbation: BIAcore Sectm1A-Fc/CD7-Fc binding; cell-surface and soluble ligand assays; T-cell IL-2/proliferation and migration assays
relation_type: exact Sectm1a-CD7 binding with unresolved CD7-specific productive signaling
pathway_branch: Sectm1a-CD7 binding; T-cell costimulation can be CD7-independent and may involve GITR/PI3K or alternate receptors
limitations: Direct mouse binding is established, but the principal functional costimulatory response was not CD7-dependent in the tested system. Human SECTM1 evidence is supportive context only and is not used to promote a mouse exact-pair relay.

cell_type_model: leukocytes; endothelial and inflammatory flow chambers; PSGL1-null mice
assay_or_perturbation: cell-adhesion and glycan-dependence assays; blocking antibodies; intravital/flow rolling; PSGL1 loss and signaling-complex assays
relation_type: exact glycan-dependent PSGL1-SELL/L-selectin adhesion with leukocyte rolling function
pathway_branch: PSGL1-SELL/L-selectin -> leukocyte tethering and rolling -> inflammatory recruitment
limitations: Binding requires PSGL1 glycosylation, tyrosine sulfation, and calcium-dependent presentation in a trans-cellular context. SELL has additional ligands, and no discrete SELL-proximal kinase relay or terminal TF is assigned.

cell_type_model: platelets; leukocytes; soluble and cell-surface PSGL1/P-selectin systems
assay_or_perturbation: calcium-dependent equilibrium binding; glycoform and sulfation analysis; flow rolling and PSGL1-deficient in vivo assays
relation_type: exact glycan-dependent PSGL1-SELP/P-selectin adhesion with platelet-leukocyte rolling function
pathway_branch: PSGL1-SELP/P-selectin -> platelet-leukocyte tethering and rolling -> inflammatory recruitment
limitations: Affinity and selectivity depend on fucosylation, sialylation, tyrosine sulfation, and multivalent cell-surface presentation. The edge is adhesion-dominant and does not establish a distinct receptor-proximal transcriptional relay.

cell_type_model: growth cones; COS cells expressing NRP1/PlexinA1; lymphatic valve endothelium
assay_or_perturbation: complex reconstitution and ligand-binding; dominant-negative PlexinA1; Sema3A-induced growth-cone collapse and lymphatic-valve assays
relation_type: exact Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA1 receptor-complex formation and signaling
pathway_branch: Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA1 -> plexin Rho/Rac/FAK-CRMP cytoskeletal signaling -> growth-cone collapse and valve morphogenesis
limitations: NRP1 supplies much of the class-3 semaphorin binding interface and PLXNA1 is the signal-transducing subunit; the pair is a complex edge, not a claim of direct Sema3A-PLXNA1 binary binding. Cellular stoichiometry is context-dependent.

cell_type_model: COS reconstitution; neuronal growth cones; purified extracellular ternary-complex system
assay_or_perturbation: PlexinA1/A2 reconstitution and collapse assays; structural Sema3A-NRP1-PLXNA2 complex analysis; receptor perturbation
relation_type: exact Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA2 ternary receptor-complex signaling
pathway_branch: Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA2 -> plexin cytoskeletal/Rho-Rac-CRMP signaling -> growth-cone collapse and axon guidance
limitations: This is a receptor-complex assignment: NRP1 is the principal ligand-binding component and PLXNA2 transduces signal. Reconstitution and structural assays do not imply that free PLXNA2 alone binds Sema3A.

cell_type_model: COS reconstitution; developing neurons; cerebellar granule neurons
assay_or_perturbation: PlexinA3/A4 reconstitution and collapse; genetic Sema3a/Plexin loss; dendritic-growth and CRMP2 assays
relation_type: exact NRP1/PLXNA3 receptor-complex contribution to Sema3A signaling, with context-dependent stoichiometry
pathway_branch: Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA3 -> CRMP2/Rho-cytoskeletal signaling -> neurite repulsion and dendritic growth
limitations: Early reconstitution assigned stronger Sema3A signaling to PlexinA1/A2 than A3, while genetic and neuronal studies support A3 contributions. NRP1/A3 is not isolated as a universal binary complex, so direct binding is not claimed.

cell_type_model: purified extracellular receptor complex; neuronal axon-guidance systems
assay_or_perturbation: cryo-EM and biochemical reconstruction of near-intact Sema3A/PLXNA4/NRP1 complex; PlexinA4 loss and neuronal guidance assays
relation_type: exact Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA4 tripartite receptor-complex formation and signaling
pathway_branch: Sema3A-NRP1/PLXNA4 -> plexin cytoskeletal/CRMP signaling -> growth-cone collapse and axon guidance
limitations: The structural result defines a 2:2:2 extracellular complex; it does not establish a free PLXNA4 binary ligand interface independent of NRP1. Downstream phenotypes are cytoskeletal and guidance endpoints, not TF measurements.

cell_type_model: pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells; endothelial cells; collective migration assays
assay_or_perturbation: Sema3D-AP binding and co-IP with PlexinD1; NRP1 dependence; Plxnd1 loss; PI3K-AKT, invasion and endothelial migration assays
relation_type: exact Sema3D-PLXND1 complex/activation with context-dependent NRP1 cooperation
pathway_branch: Sema3D-NRP1/PLXND1 -> context-specific PI3K-AKT/RhoA-cytoskeletal signaling -> pancreatic invasion or endothelial migration
limitations: Direct binding is weak and enhanced by NRP1/secretory context; ANXA2-dependent cancer signaling and endothelial studies disagree on PLXND1 requirement. The exact pair is supported, but no universal stoichiometry or relay is claimed.

cell_type_model: vascular endothelium; thymocytes; striatal neurons; endothelial migration models
assay_or_perturbation: purified Sema3E/PLXND1 SPR and pull-down; genetic Plxnd1 loss; migration, vascular patterning, synapse and actin/focal-adhesion assays
relation_type: exact Sema3E-PLXND1 ligand binding and receptor-proximal signaling
pathway_branch: Sema3E-PLXND1 -> RhoA/actin and focal-adhesion signaling -> vascular patterning, thymocyte migration and synapse formation
limitations: Sema3E processing, cell type, and neuropilin independence vary by model. The exact receptor edge is direct, but downstream outputs are context-specific and not transcription-factor endpoints.

cell_type_model: U87MG glioma cells; HUVECs; lymphatic endothelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: Sema3F stimulation; NRP2/PLXNA1 complex and receptor perturbation; ABL2/p190RhoGAP, RhoA, cytoskeletal collapse, migration and lymphatic assays
relation_type: exact Sema3F-NRP2/PLXNA1 receptor-complex signaling
pathway_branch: Sema3F-NRP2/PLXNA1 -> ABL2/p190RhoGAP-RhoA inactivation -> cytoskeletal collapse and migration inhibition
limitations: The principal ligand-binding subunit is NRP2 and PLXNA1 is the signal-transducing component; overexpression/heterologous models affect stoichiometry. Some lymphatic phenotypes involve PlexinA3 or additional plexins, which are not transferred here.

cell_type_model: COS-cell receptor reconstitution; lymphatic endothelial cells; developing neural systems
assay_or_perturbation: older reconstitution/cell-contraction reports compared with later class-3 semaphorin specificity and loss-of-function studies
relation_type: conflicting NRP2-PLXNA2 receptor-complex assignment; no resolved exact Sema3F-NRP2/PLXNA2 relay
pathway_branch: Sema3F-NRP2/PLXNA1 or PLXNA3 is supported; NRP2/PLXNA2 remains a negative/competing boundary rather than a promoted exact edge
limitations: Early reconstitution literature and reviews report NRP2/PLXNA2-associated collapse, whereas later exact ligand/receptor specificity and lymphatic studies support Sema3F with PlexinA1/A3 and implicate PlexinA2 in other class-3 semaphorin contexts. No robust exact-pair direct binding plus isolated downstream relay resolves the conflict; family analogy is not used.
